rules.statement: Do not skip, disable, or weaken existing tests (e.g. adding Skip attributes, deleting assertions, loosening expected values) to make a change pass.
rules.why: The source treats skipped or weakened tests as a shortcut that hides real failures; that makes it a review finding even when the checks pass.
rules.check: Look for tests that were newly skipped or ignored, removed or commented-out assertions, broadened expectations, or deleted test cases in the diff that have no stated reason.

rules.statement: Do not swallow exceptions or errors; a caught error must be handled, rethrown, or reported, never silently ignored.
rules.why: The source names swallowed errors as a shortcut that hides failures and must be flagged.
rules.check: Look for empty catch blocks, catch blocks that only return a default value, or ignored error results that are not logged, rethrown, or turned into a meaningful outcome.

rules.statement: Do not leave TODO or placeholder comments in place of required behavior in a finished change.
rules.why: The source names leftover TODOs as a shortcut showing the work was not done as written.
rules.check: Search the added lines for TODO, FIXME, HACK, or NotImplementedException placeholders that stand in for behavior the change was meant to deliver.

rules.statement: Do not hard-code values that should come from inputs, configuration, or computation just to satisfy a test or a specific case.
rules.why: The source names hard-coded values as a shortcut that makes a change look correct without implementing the real behavior.
rules.check: Look for literal values in production code that copy test expectations, special-case one particular input, or replace a value that should come from configuration or parameters.
